artifacts.summary: Verifies the four disagreeing handoff schemas against the freshly-redeployed source store, finds the readers already reconciled with each other but a live artifact-linking defect in the only active writer, and recommends: one JSON Schema file, delete skill_write_orchestrator_handoff and make .return-meta.json the base-mode channel, canonicalize the hard/wrap-up.md blocker shape and flat continuation_path form, and expand validate-handoff.sh's status enum plus add an artifacts check.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system's orchestrator-handoff contract, always cross-check a documented schema against actual reader jq paths via grep before trusting the prose doc: handoff-schema.md's own 'Complete JSON Schema' example omitted skeleton/sorry_inventory/artifacts[].summary and documented a blockers shape ({description,phase,severity}) that neither orchestrate engine (base or hard) ever reads -- only the wrap-up.md hard shape ({phase,target,verbatim_goal,...}) is read, and only by the hard engine. Grepping for '.field[0].subfield' reader patterns across both SKILL.md engines is the fast way to find which documented shape is actually live vs dead.

general-implementation-hard-agent.md's Stage 5 H9 handoff-write template omits 'summary' and 'artifacts' entirely, even though both skill-orchestrate and skill-orchestrate-hard unconditionally read '.summary' and '.artifacts[0].path' from every handoff to decide whether to call skill_link_artifacts. This means live hard-mode implement dispatches never get their summary artifact auto-linked into state.json today -- a silent defect, not just a documentation gap. Worth checking for analogous 'engine reads a field the only live writer's own written template omits' gaps whenever auditing a handoff/return-channel contract.
